questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: That it was not too far away. I wanted to explore new cultures, but traveling outside europe made things way more complicated. I have a personal connection to Holland, so Amsterdam was the ideal choice.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Easy. Vrije University were extremely helpful and always fast to respond.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: A lot. They had scavenger hunt of both the campus and one in Amsterdam central to get to know the city. They made it easy to connect with other exchange students.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I found housing through DUWO. There is a lot of competition to get a room, so you have to be very fast and keep up with your email inbox. They let you know the time slot, and then you just have to be ready at that time.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: If you study at Vride University renting a room at Uilenstede (DUWO) is very ideal, Although it is a little fa from center (7km), it is 2 km from uni, and everybody lives there + the rent is very fair.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I chose the room with private bathroom which is very recommended! I still shared to kitchen with 13 other. We had a really great community in my kitchen, and in my opinion this is the best option.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I registered from home.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: They had an email, were they would respond pretty fast. I used them a lot as it was i bit confusing which classes I was allowed to take.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Semi. This was a bit of a struggle and not very transparrend by the webside. It all worked out though.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Honestly there are limited options. I wanted to have 2 classes in period 4, two classes in period 5 and 1 in period 6. They didn't offer any in period 6, why I had to take 3 classes in period 4, which was brutal but I got through it.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Many of my courses were pretty interesting. The students, in my opinion, are very lazy though and in all of my group work I was always the one doing the most. I found that very strange as my grade does not really matter here, as it just gets converted to "passed". I thing in general this is a problem of the VU, but then again when you are on exchange it is nice the don't have high expectations.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I took a mix of BA and MA courses.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: I would say the style is quite similar. There are more closed book exams than at UPCH. The style varied a lot from class to class, which is also the case in UCPH. In one class i had to memorise 600 pages plus all lecture slides for a 6 point class (??), and others were way more chill.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Behavior and Communication in Organizations
Beyond Gender Inequalities 
Improving Planetary Health
Persuasive Communication
Privacy, Self-Disclosure and Big Data

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Behavior and Communication in Organizations (interesting, but a lot of reading)
Improving Planetary Health
Persuasive Communication

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: In DUWO you have to rent to room till mid august. It is sooooo difficult to get a room though so it is worth it.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Books are expensive but some you could find online.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: VU had a sportscenter which was really nice. There gym space was super good, and they had a ton of classes (everything from spinning to pole dance). Also ESN host so many things so there are always things to do and people to meet.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: VU sportscenter.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: For sure explore all the cities around Amsterdam. Holland is just the cutest country.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: No problem.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Honestly I found this very difficult, as the ones I were in work groups with did the bare minimum. I found all my friends from the ESN things and where i lived.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: I am very are used to bike in Copenhagen, but bike culture in Amsterdam is a new level. They don't use hand signaling and no one cares about if the light is red or green - as soon as you get the hang of it though, it is no problem!

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Just how pretty it is.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Get a room with DUWO at Uilenstede with private bathroom, shared kitchen - stay on top of your inbox for notifications!
Rent a Swapfiets - all around great service
Get a Museum Card

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: no.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Being able to find really close friendships from around the world. I am at the final year of my master (25 years old), and I was afraid that I would not connect with anyone, because generally people are a few years younger when they go on exchange. While I for sure was the oldest, connecting with people was not a problem at all.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The first moth of adjusting and having high expectations of what you are supposed to be doing. Take it easy, a feeling of home and close friendships does not form overnight -  be kind to yourself!

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
